name: Islamic State
note: The Islamic State while it holds territory: administration, revenue, forces, a consolidation or expansion strategy, provinces abroad, an insurgency branch for after 2017 and an alternative-history branch for a state that survives past 2019. Neutral and descriptive; the group's rise and fall is scripted in data/events/conflicts.json, and the counterfactual branches are for the player or off-history games only.

focuses.name: A proto-state
focuses.description: The group organises an administration in the towns it holds, after proclaiming a caliphate in 2014.

focuses.name: Town councils
focuses.description: Councils run the towns and the districts around them.

focuses.name: Courts
focuses.description: Courts replace the state's courts in the territory.

focuses.name: Water, power and bread
focuses.description: Keep the waterworks, power stations and bakeries running.

focuses.name: Tax offices
focuses.description: Offices collect levies on trade and farming.

focuses.name: Records and registers
focuses.description: Registers of land, property and residents.

focuses.name: Repair crews
focuses.description: Crews repair roads and power lines in the territory.

focuses.name: Ease the strain
focuses.description: More officials and simpler rules for the administration.

focuses.name: Internal police
focuses.description: A police force patrols the towns.

focuses.name: Schools and clinics
focuses.description: The administration takes over schools and clinics.

focuses.name: The dinar
focuses.description: Issue the group's own coinage, the dinar, used from 2014 to 2019.

focuses.name: Provincial administration
focuses.description: The territory is divided into provinces with their own administrations.

focuses.name: Tribal agreements
focuses.description: Agreements with tribes in the Euphrates valley.

focuses.name: Revenue
focuses.description: Pay for the group from the territory it holds. By the end of 2015 its budget was over US$1 billion.

focuses.name: The oil fields
focuses.description: Run the oil fields in the territory. Unlocks oil sales.

focuses.name: Seized banks
focuses.description: Take over the bank branches in the captured cities.

focuses.name: Makeshift refineries
focuses.description: Small refineries turn crude into fuel.

focuses.name: A war economy
focuses.description: Oil, levies and seized assets fund the war.

focuses.name: Farms of the Euphrates
focuses.description: Wheat and barley from the irrigated valley.

focuses.name: Trade routes
focuses.description: Fuel and goods move through the borderlands.

focuses.name: Workshops
focuses.description: Workshops repair vehicles and make spare parts.

focuses.name: Grain stores
focuses.description: Silos and mills store the harvest.

focuses.name: A budget office
focuses.description: One office plans revenue and spending across the provinces.

focuses.name: Forces
focuses.description: Organise the group's fighters into an army.

focuses.name: Captured arsenals
focuses.description: Use the weapons and vehicles left in army depots.

focuses.name: Recruitment
focuses.description: Recruit fighters in the territory. Unlocks recruitment drives.

focuses.name: Training camps
focuses.description: Camps train new recruits.

focuses.name: Mobile columns
focuses.description: Fast columns of light vehicles.

focuses.name: Foreign recruits
focuses.description: Recruits arrive from abroad.

focuses.name: Former officers
focuses.description: Experienced officers command the units.

focuses.name: Artillery
focuses.description: Captured guns and mortars form artillery units.

focuses.name: Defend the cities
focuses.description: Fortify the cities against offensives. Unlocks city defences.

focuses.name: Explosives workshops
focuses.description: Workshops make mines and explosives for defence.

focuses.name: Drones
focuses.description: Small commercial drones for scouting and attack.

focuses.name: Adapt to the air campaign
focuses.description: Disperse, hide vehicles and move at night. Coalition airstrikes began in Iraq on 8 August 2014 and in Syria on 22 September 2014.

focuses.name: Anti-aircraft guns
focuses.description: Guns and missiles against helicopters and aircraft.

focuses.name: Elite units
focuses.description: Experienced units for the hardest fighting.

focuses.name: Strategy
focuses.description: Hold what the group has or push on.

focuses.name: Consolidation
focuses.description: Hold Mosul and Raqqa, fortify the territory and administer it.

focuses.name: Defence lines
focuses.description: Trenches, berms and minefields around the cities.

focuses.name: Hold Mosul
focuses.description: Mosul, taken between 4 and 10 June 2014, is the largest city the group holds.

focuses.name: Hold Raqqa
focuses.description: Raqqa, held since January 2014, is the seat of the administration.

focuses.name: Under siege
focuses.description: Prepare the cities for long sieges: stores, tunnels and shelters.

focuses.name: Expansion
focuses.description: Push toward Baghdad and Damascus.

focuses.name: Claims in Iraq
focuses.description: Mark the next targets along the front.

focuses.name: Offensive columns
focuses.description: Columns for a new offensive.

focuses.name: Claims in Syria
focuses.description: Mark targets toward the west.

focuses.name: Total mobilisation
focuses.description: Every town sends men to the front.

focuses.name: Open new fronts
focuses.description: Attack where the enemy is weakest. Unlocks new fronts.

focuses.name: Hold the line
focuses.description: Whatever the strategy, keep the front.

focuses.name: Provinces abroad
focuses.description: Groups in other countries pledge allegiance and are named provinces of the group.

focuses.name: Libya Province
focuses.description: Three branches in Libya were formed on 13 November 2014.

focuses.name: Sinai Province
focuses.description: A group in the Sinai became a province of the group during 2014.

focuses.name: Khorasan Province
focuses.description: A province for Afghanistan and Pakistan was announced on 26 January 2015.

focuses.name: The Greater Sahara
focuses.description: A group in the Sahel, formed on 15 May 2015, joins the network.

focuses.name: A network abroad
focuses.description: Couriers and money link the provinces abroad.

focuses.name: Outlast the centre
focuses.description: The provinces abroad keep the group alive if the centre falls.

focuses.name: After the caliphate
focuses.description: Prepare for the loss of the cities: cells, hideouts and stores in the desert.

focuses.name: Desert hideouts
focuses.description: Hideouts and supply routes across the desert between Iraq and Syria.

focuses.name: Go underground
focuses.description: Units break up into cells.

focuses.name: Hidden stores
focuses.description: Weapons and money stored in hiding places.

focuses.name: Courier networks
focuses.description: Messages travel by courier, not phone.

focuses.name: Rural cells
focuses.description: Small cells in the countryside of Iraq and Syria, an insurgency that began in 2017.

focuses.name: Recover
focuses.description: Rebuild the organisation from the cells.

focuses.name: Regroup in the desert
focuses.description: Larger units form again in the desert.

focuses.name: A surviving state
focuses.description: Alternative history: the group still holds its cities after the offensives of 2016 to 2019 and runs them as a state.

focuses.name: Permanent ministries
focuses.description: Offices become ministries with fixed budgets and staff.

focuses.name: Rebuild the cities
focuses.description: Rebuild housing, roads and markets in the cities held.

focuses.name: Border defences
focuses.description: Fortified lines along the borders of the territory.

focuses.name: A state budget
focuses.description: An annual budget with revenue and spending plans.

focuses.name: Factories
focuses.description: Reopen factories in the cities.

focuses.name: A standing army
focuses.description: Units become a standing army with ranks and barracks.

focuses.name: Oil exports
focuses.description: Repair the oil fields and pipelines for steady exports.

focuses.name: Arms factories
focuses.description: Produce weapons and ammunition at home.

focuses.name: An officer academy
focuses.description: Train officers for the standing army.

focuses.name: Trade routes
focuses.description: Trade with the neighbouring regions.

focuses.name: Internal consolidation
focuses.description: Fewer offices, clearer rules and a calmer territory.

focuses.name: A drone programme
focuses.description: Build drones at home.

focuses.name: Talks with neighbours
focuses.description: Indirect talks on prisoners, water and trade. No state recognises the group.

focuses.name: An entrenched state
focuses.description: The territory is run as a state behind fortified borders.
